meta.bands: ELELex carries frequencies per level, not an expert level, so 1-3 are A1, A2 and B1 as the first level at which at least 3 different coursebooks use the lemma; proper nouns (FreeLing NP), interjections other than a few greetings (hola, adiós), multiword entries and a few names tagged as common nouns (maría) are left out; `gracia` is taken as `gracias`. 4-6 are rank buckets of 800 over the frequency tail, which no list covers, with everything already in bands 1-3 removed. Latin American Spanish is the target; the sources are pan-Hispanic, and the tail is checked against the Mexican dictionary.

meta.filtered: Bands 4-6 only, except the vulgarity block, which bands 1-3 pass through as well since ELELex is counted rather than chosen; it also takes `coger`, vulgar in Mexico. A tail word must be a lower-case entry of the Mexican Spanish Hunspell dictionary, which drops most names, and a common-noun lemma somewhere in ELELex at any level, since the dictionary also lists inflected forms (fue, estoy, dime) as entries; a known given name is dropped as well, and so is a word ranking five times better in English subtitles than in Spanish ones, which is a line nobody translated. Interjections, slurs and strong vulgarity, words shorter than three letters, words holding a hyphen or a space and words the Lexicon's suffix reduction already lands on a word held here are dropped too.
meta.source: ELELex (François, Göbel, Lundquist et al., CEFRLex project), lemma frequencies in Spanish-as-a-foreign-language coursebooks by CEFR level, as bands 1-3; OpenSubtitles 2018 frequency (Lison & Tiedemann) rank buckets as bands 4-6
